The Quiet Lighthouse

By A. Writer

The lighthouse on the northern cape has been dark for eleven years, but the keeper still climbs its stairs every evening. He says the habit keeps his knees honest and his mind clear.

Visitors arrive most summers, curious about the man who tends a light that no longer shines. Some bring coffee; others bring questions about the storms, the ships, and the long winters.

"People think it is lonely," he said, "but the sea is never quiet enough to be lonely." He laughed, then pointed toward the horizon where a fishing boat was turning for home.

Engineers have proposed restoring the lamp with modern equipment. The keeper supports the idea, although he admits that the darkness has its own kind of beauty.
